_guide.purpose: Drives the in-app 'What's New' popup. After every release, add a new object at the TOP of `versions`.
rules: 2. Bump PATCH (1.0.7 -> 1.0.8) for bug fixes, PERF, security. Bump MINOR (1.0.x -> 1.1.0) for new features. Bump MAJOR (1.x -> 2.0.0) for breaking changes.
3. Every change is tagged to a module via `app`. The popup only shows a module to users who have access to it.

4. `app` must be a valid id from APP_ACCESS_CONFIG in assets/app.js (dpr, planning, quality, hr, masters, purchase, supervisor_app, ...). Use app: 'all' for platform-wide notes (performance, security, login) that everyone should see.
5. `type` is one of: feat | fix | perf | security | improvement. It renders as a coloured pill.
6. Keep each change one clear sentence written for a factory user, not a developer. No commit hashes.
7. `date` is the release date in YYYY-MM-DD.

versions.title: Machine data popup now shows shots produced per hour
versions.summary: Clicking the machine counter on a DPR hour cell now shows how many shots the machine produced in that hour (the counter's rise over the hour), plus the total counter and the real cycle time. Fields that this controller does not report accurately (cavity, shot weight) have been removed so only trustworthy numbers are shown.

changes.text: The machine-counter popup now leads with shots produced in that hour, and no longer shows fields the machine does not report correctly.

versions.title: Machine data now reads the live KEBA controllers correctly
versions.summary: First on-machine commissioning of the machine-data feature. The KEBA controllers send their values as decimals rather than the whole-number format the manual described, so counter and cycle time were decoded wrongly. This corrects the decoding (verified against the machine showing 205 shots at 33.9s), and makes the collector tolerant of controllers that only expose part of the register range.

changes.text: The machine counter and cycle time now show correct values instead of very large numbers, matching what the machine's own screen shows.

versions.title: Machines can now report their counter and cycle time to JMS automatically
versions.summary: Moulding machines with a KEBA controller can be connected to JMS over the factory network. Once a machine's IP is set in Masters, its shot counter and cycle time are collected automatically and shown next to the manually entered figures — so you can check accuracy before relying on it. Nothing is written into DPR automatically, so manual entry stays the record.

changes.text: A machine can now be linked to its controller by entering its IP address in the machine's settings, so JMS can collect live data from it.
Each hour cell shows the machine's own counter beside the entered figure; click it to see cavity, shot weight, cycle time and when the last reading was taken.
A live panel shows connected machines with their current counter, cycle time and running/stopped status.

versions.title: Weight checks widened to 10%, and the sync health alert now tells the truth
versions.summary: Supervisor weight tolerance moves from 5% to 10% and the DPR Compliance Summary flags parts that fall outside it. Behind the scenes, the hourly sync health check has been repaired — it had been failing on a connection fault for weeks while reporting it as a stale factory server.

changes.text: Part weight is now accepted within 10% of standard instead of 5%, so normal shot-to-shot variation stops being flagged as a problem.
DPR Compliance Summary now marks entries whose weight is over or under the allowed band, so out-of-spec parts stand out at a glance.
Import from ERP Data now shows the first 5,000 changes at a time — confirm those, then press it again for the rest. Very large first-time imports no longer risk failing part-way.
Searching OR/JR Status and Job Card reports now matches what you typed — the search was previously adding stray spaces and missing rows.
The automatic sync health alert works again. It had been failing to reach the server and reporting that as a stale factory server, which sent people to check the wrong machine.
When the health check cannot reach the server it now says so plainly, instead of blaming a factory sync it never managed to check.

versions.title: Set quantities can be corrected again, and the ERP import now covers every factory
versions.summary: Correcting the Plan Qty on a plan for a multi-piece set no longer fails with an 'exceeds the limit' error. The ERP import now brings in Factory 2's orders, which were being left out, and gets dates right. Job Card approvals can no longer half-save.

changes.text: Correcting a plan's quantity on a multi-piece set now works. Plan Qty is checked against that mould's own Mould Item Qty and Job Qty against the order's set quantity, so a 7-piece set ordered as 1800 sets correctly allows 10800 pieces on a 6-up mould instead of refusing it.
Quantity already planned is now counted per mould, so the body, lid and basket of one set no longer eat into each other's allowance.
The Edit Plan window shows both limits side by side — Mould Item Qty in pieces and OR Qty in sets — with the maximum allowed per colour for each.

A Job Card approval that fails now leaves the plan exactly where it was. Previously the plan could quietly move to the next stage while the screen reported an error, and a double-click could apply two approvals.
Factory 2 (Shivani) orders now come through the ERP import. They were being left out because the factory could not be matched by name.
Imported OR and Job Card dates can no longer land a day early or late.
The import preview now lists only the rows the save will really change, instead of reporting changes to remarks that were never applied.
Text arriving from the ERP is now displayed safely in the import review screen.

versions.title: OR-JR Status can now be filled from the ERP instead of an Excel upload
versions.summary: Masters -> OR-JR Status has a new "Import from ERP Data" button. It brings in JR Status data already fetched from the ERP, showing you exactly what is new and what changed before anything is saved. Only your own factory's orders are brought in. The Excel upload still works if you need it.

changes.text: New "Import from ERP Data" button on OR-JR Status fills the report from ERP data — no more downloading an Excel from the ERP and uploading it by hand.
The import only brings in orders belonging to the factory you are logged into; orders from the other plants are counted and left out.
Before saving, you see the same review screen as the Excel upload, listing every new and changed row so nothing is written without you approving it.
The screen shows when the ERP data was last fetched, and warns you if it is more than a day old so you can ask a superadmin to refresh it.
A blank Remarks value can no longer wipe the Remarks already saved against an order — this applies to the Excel upload as well.

versions.title: Plan approvals no longer fail on the factory server
versions.summary: Approving a plan on a factory (LOCAL) server could fail with a database duplicate-key error, leaving the plan stuck in Pending Plan Approval. The server now keeps its internal record numbering in step with records received from the main server.

changes.text: Approving a plan from Pending Plan Approval no longer fails with a duplicate-key error on factory servers — the approval saves and the plan moves on as expected.
Factory servers now re-align their internal record numbering after receiving data from the main server, preventing duplicate-record errors when saving new entries.

versions.title: Job Card approval can no longer be skipped from the Machine Timeline
versions.summary: Marking 'JC Given', setting a P1-P4 priority, or starting a plan now always requires a linked Job Card that has been approved by both PPC and Moulding. Removing JC Given or clearing a priority still works as before.

changes.text: 'JC Given' can only be ticked after a Job Card is linked and both PPC and Moulding have approved the plan — the box stays greyed out until then.
Setting a machine priority (P1-P4) or starting a plan is blocked until the Job Card approval is complete, with a message telling you which approval is still pending.
Priorities that were already set earlier keep working; only new assignments need the completed approval.

versions.title: Fix: changing a plan's mould now works even when the correct mould is already planned
versions.summary: In the superadmin Edit Plan window, correcting a plan to a mould that is already planned for the same OR used to show an error. It now applies cleanly.

changes.text: Edit Plan: you can now correct a plan to a mould that is already planned for the same OR without getting an error.

versions.title: New Machine Maintenance Report — see which machines lose the most hours to maintenance
versions.summary: Reports gets a Machine Maintenance Report: pick Daily, Weekly or Monthly and a date range, and see machine-wise maintenance downtime in hours, with the most-affected machines highlighted on top. Exports to Excel/CSV.

changes.text: New Machine Maintenance Report: choose Daily, Weekly or Monthly and a date range to see maintenance downtime machine-wise, in hours and minutes.
A summary on top shows total maintenance downtime, how many machines were affected, and each machine's total — most-affected machines first.
Counts maintenance from both supervisor quick actions and downtime reasons logged inside production entries, so nothing is missed.

versions.title: DPR now predicts each shift's final tonnage — per machine, per line, and plant-wide
versions.summary: While a shift is running, the Compliance Summary shows how many pieces and how many kg each machine is expected to finish with by shift end, based on its actual speed so far. Line headers and the Plant Total card show the same prediction added up.

changes.text: Each machine's summary box now shows a Pred line — the pieces and kg that machine is expected to reach by the end of the selected shift, based on its actual speed so far (or the standard rate if the shift just started).
Every line header shows the predicted total kg for that line, and the Plant Total card at the top gets a new Pred. Tonnage figure for the whole plant.
The prediction respects maintenance windows and completed moulds — those hours are not counted — and it only appears while the shift still has hours left.

versions.title: PPC can now allow extra production beyond the 10% limit — with a full record of who allowed what and why
versions.summary: When a colour hits its 10% over-production block, PPC/Planner/Admin can allow extra quantity for that colour from the Machine Timeline, with a written reason. Supervisors see who allowed the extra, and a new report lists every allowance.

changes.text: In the Machine Timeline colour view, PPC managers, planners and admins get a new Allow button to permit extra quantity for a colour beyond the 10% cap — a reason is compulsory.
The colour table shows how much extra was allowed and by whom, with the reason on hover, plus the full history of earlier allowances.
When PPC allows extra quantity for a colour, the entry limit increases automatically and the colour table shows a badge with the allowed extra and the name of who allowed it.
The over-production block message now tells the supervisor to ask PPC for extra allowance from the Machine Timeline, instead of a dead end.

New report: Extra Allowed QTY By PPC — every allowance with who allowed it, against which order/job/plan, which colour, how much, and the written reason, with totals per person and per colour. Exports to Excel/CSV.

versions.title: Job Detail gets a trend chart, and machines that go quiet raise an alert
versions.summary: The DPR Job Detail window is redesigned with a progress ring, an hourly trend chart with target line and estimated finish time, and over-produced quantities are now shown instead of a zero balance. The Compliance Summary warns when a machine has no entry for the last 3 hours.

changes.text: When a colour is produced above its plan, the Balance column now shows how many pieces OVER it went (in blue) instead of showing 0.
New hourly Production Trend chart in the Job Detail window — produced, rejected and downtime per hour, with the target rate line and day/night markers.
The Job Detail window now predicts when the job will finish, based on the last few hours' actual speed, and warns when the machine is running behind target.
The Job Detail window has a cleaner look: a progress ring, clear stat tiles, and pie charts for downtime and rejection reasons.

The Compliance Summary shows a red alert when a machine has had NO production entry for the last 3 hours — with a banner on top, a blinking mark on the machine row, and a small popup with that machine's colour-wise production while you scroll.

Every machine row now shows small badges when that machine did a Mould Change (yellow MC), Colour Change (orange CC) or Job Change (blue/red JC) — so changes are visible at a glance without opening entries.

versions.title: Downtime on production hours now shows as a split box

changes.text: When a production hour also has supervisor downtime, the box now splits in two — quantity and colour on top, the downtime reason with its minutes in a coloured strip below, instead of the small badge that was hard to read.
Downtime reasons that don't have their own signboard colour now show in a neutral grey strip with the minutes, instead of plain pink hours.

versions.title: Maintenance hours are now yellow, like the factory signboard

changes.text: Machine Maintenance hours in the Compliance Summary are now yellow with the maintenance tools icon — the same colour as the signboard on the machine.
Every downtime reason now shows its icon inside a small round sign, so the grid reads like the boards on the shop floor.
When an hour has both production and a short downtime, the box now splits in two — quantity on top and the downtime reason with its minutes below, easy to read without opening the entry.

versions.title: Supervisor entry checks stop over-count and wrong setup values
versions.summary: The Supervisor app now guards production entry: cavity can't exceed the mould's standard, article weight must stay within ±5% of standard, and colour-wise entry is capped at 10% over the planned quantity so a colour can't be over-produced.

changes.text: Actual Cavity can no longer be saved higher than the mould's Standard Cavity.
Actual article weight must be within ±5% of the standard weight — the allowed range is shown if an entry is outside it.

Colour-wise production is capped at 10% over that colour's planned quantity: a colour planned for 500 can take at most 550 across all entries, and the colour picker shows how many more pieces are allowed.
When a colour reaches its limit the app explains it clearly instead of showing a confusing zero, and unplanned colours are left uncapped.

versions.title: See why a machine was down right on the DPR summary
versions.summary: The DPR Compliance Summary now shows an icon and name for every downtime reason, and hour slots that had both production and downtime show a small badge with the reason and minutes — no need to open the entry.

changes.text: Machine Maintenance, Manpower Shortage, No Plan, Mould Maintenance and Mould Trial hours now show a clear icon with the reason name in the summary grid.
When an hour has production and downtime together, the slot shows a small badge with the downtime reason and minutes — point at it to see the full breakup.
The filter bar shows a legend of the new reason icons, and the View Filter list shows matching symbols.

versions.title: Supervisor app updates itself and never blocks your taps
versions.summary: The Supervisor app now picks up new fixes on its own, and the Processing popup can always be dismissed with one tap.

changes.text: The app now checks for updates on its own and refreshes itself when a fix is released — no need to close and reopen it. It never refreshes while you are typing an entry.
Tapping the Processing popup now always dismisses it — it can no longer jump straight back onto the screen.

versions.title: Sync alerts now name the factory that stopped syncing
versions.summary: Behind the scenes: when a factory's local server stops sending data to the main server, the automatic alert email now says exactly which factory it is and for how long — so the problem gets fixed faster.

changes.text: Sync health alert emails now name the exact factory server that stopped syncing and how long ago its last update was, instead of a generic warning.
The alert also tells apart a stopped factory server from the main server being down, so the right thing gets checked first.

versions.title: Supervisor submit no longer gets stuck on Processing
versions.summary: Submitting a DPR entry on the Supervisor app no longer leaves the Processing popup stuck on screen — you see Saved right away and can move to the next hour.

changes.text: After tapping Submit DPR, the Processing popup used to stay stuck for 15–30 seconds on slow Wi-Fi. It now closes as soon as the entry is saved.
Background checks after a save no longer freeze the whole screen — the setup card shows its own small Checking message instead.
If the network is too slow to confirm a save, the app now tells you clearly to check the slot list before submitting again, instead of showing a technical error.

versions.title: Machine queue follows your P1-P4 priority
versions.summary: The plan order you set with P1-P4 priorities now drives the schedule everywhere — card order, dates, and the Mould Change Report all tell the same story.

changes.text: Machine Timeline dates now follow the P1-P4 priority order you set on plans, so the card shown second also runs second — no more dates jumping between cards.
Excel View Timeline now uses the same realistic expected-finish chaining as the Machine Timeline.
The Mould Change Report detects changes in the same priority order, so its times and the timeline's Mould Change badges always agree.

versions.title: Mould change day runs 8 AM to 8 AM
versions.summary: The Mould Change Report now follows the factory day, and timeline cards spell out Mould Change clearly.

changes.text: Selecting a date in the Mould Change Report now shows every change from 8:00 AM that day to 8:00 AM the next morning, so early-morning changes are no longer missing from today's sheet.
Machine Timeline and Excel View Timeline cards now say 'Mould Change' in full instead of the short code 'CHG'.

versions.title: Faster, safer DPR entry on the supervisor screen
versions.summary: No more double entries from double-taps or weak WiFi, Fill DPR now lands on the colour picker first, and the job list refreshes without freezing the screen.

changes.text: Tapping Submit twice, or a weak WiFi retry, can no longer save the same hour's entry two times.
The Submit button greys out while saving and comes back on its own, so a failed save can always be retried.
Fill DPR now scrolls to the Colour Breakdown so you pick the colour first before entering data.
The job list refreshes in the background — the screen no longer freezes with a full-screen Processing message.

versions.title: Better Daily Mould Change Report
versions.summary: The Mould Change Report is now a complete, print-ready sheet with accurate times, serial numbers, signatures and an Excel download.

changes.text: The Mould Change Report now shows correct realistic times even when opened directly, without visiting the Machine Timeline first.
The report is a proper daily sheet: company header, serial numbers, and a signature section for PPC, the mould change team, and the production head.
Printing now repeats the column headings on every page and never splits a row across two pages.
New Excel button downloads the loaded report as a spreadsheet.

versions.title: Realistic machine schedule and mould change times
versions.summary: The Machine Timeline and Mould Change Report now follow the machine's real production speed, so upcoming plans and mould changes show realistic dates instead of standard-speed estimates that could already be in the past.

changes.text: Queued plans on the Machine Timeline now start from the previous plan's expected finish (based on actual balance quantity), so a slow-running plan pushes the whole queue to realistic dates.
The Daily Mould Change Report shows mould change times that match the Machine Timeline, so the printed sheet no longer lists changes at times that have already passed.

versions.title: Correct a plan after it's created
versions.summary: Superadmins can now fix the quantity and colour breakdown of a plan that was already created, without deleting and re-making it.

changes.text: Superadmins get an Edit Plan button on each plan to correct the quantity and per-colour breakdown after the plan was created; every change is logged.

versions.title: Smoother, lighter interface
versions.summary: Removed heavy background effects so pages feel snappier, especially when scrolling large tables.

changes.text: Stopped a constantly-animating page background that was quietly slowing down every screen.
Made scrolling through big tables smoother by simplifying row hover and scrollbar styling.

versions.title: Reliable menu on phones & tablets
versions.summary: The side menu now slides in from a hamburger button on phones, tablets, and zoomed-in screens instead of disappearing.

changes.text: The side menu no longer vanishes on small screens or when the page is zoomed in — tap the menu button at the top-left to slide it open.
Tap the dimmed area or press Escape to close the menu; pages now scroll normally with the bottom bar in place.

versions.title: Security hardening
versions.summary: Removed credentials that were accidentally stored in the app's code and tightened protections so it can't happen again.

changes.text: Removed database and service passwords that were accidentally saved inside the application files.
Backup and maintenance tools now ask for the database password instead of storing it.

versions.title: Faster page loads (fix)
versions.summary: Fixed the faster app scripts not building on the live server.

changes.text: Fixed the smaller app script not being generated during the live build, so pages now load correctly and faster.

versions.title: Faster page loads (part 2)
versions.summary: Pages now serve the smaller, faster app scripts everywhere — including on the live server.

changes.text: Pages now load the minified app script, so every screen loads faster on all servers.

versions.title: Faster page loads
versions.summary: Pages now load quicker and work fully offline on the factory server.

changes.text: Made the app scripts smaller so pages load faster, especially on slower connections.
Fonts and the logo now load from our own server — no outside downloads, so the app is faster and works offline.

versions.title: ORJR Wise Summary row delete
versions.summary: You can now remove individual rows from the ORJR Wise Summary, just like the ORJR Wise Detail view.

changes.text: Added a delete button on each ORJR Wise Summary row so you can remove a single row you no longer need.

versions.title: What's New notifications
versions.summary: The app now tells you exactly what changed after every update — tailored to the modules you use.

changes.text: After every update, a 'What's New' popup shows the changes for the modules you have access to.
Click the version number at the bottom of the sidebar any time to re-read the latest release notes.

versions.title: Stability & Quality
versions.summary: Fixes across the Daily Production Report and Quality modules, plus a supervisor entry fix.

changes.text: Fixed the Daily Production Report crashing and showing a blank page.
Corrected reports that were showing zero target and zero efficiency.
Compliance View filter now correctly includes machines stopped for MP Shortage, Maintenance and other downtime reasons.
Fixed First Piece Approval (FPA) images not displaying.
Added new panels to the Quality Dashboard for a clearer at-a-glance view.
Cleaned up unused screens for a faster, tidier module.
Stopped the quick-action auto-fill from carrying forward after you make a manual Main entry.

versions.title: Planning & Supervisor upgrades
versions.summary: New Planning tools, a redesigned supervisor entry experience, and automatic factory-server updates.

changes.text: Added a High Priority Job Sheet to the Planning Board.
New Recent Slots panel to quickly reopen your recent entries.
Redesigned entry cards with clearer type badges and better layout on mobile.
Fixed reject/downtime chips and the header Line chip overflowing on small screens.
Factory local servers now update themselves automatically from the main server.
New Activity Monitor shows real-time user activity across all JMS Ocean apps.

versions.title: Performance & QC redesign
versions.summary: A major speed-up across the platform and a refreshed Quality Control experience.

changes.text: Made pages load noticeably faster by fixing slow database queries and adding indexes on hot paths.
Hardened session handling with secure random session IDs.
Redesigned QC with compact cards, a machine-sorted queue, and a mandatory FPA -> Setup -> QC flow.
Added an image gallery and verify-from-queue for faster inspections.
